task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: lineup coverage of structural roles (organizer, shaper, terminal)
separability of role coverage from talent and possession counts
talent control in lineup-level influence measures
methodological_questions: Is lineup role coverage separable from player talent and usage/count confounds?
Does talent control behave adequately when role coverage varies within team?
What reliability and sample-size constraints apply to lineup-level role coverage across team-seasons?
evidence_establishes: The retrieval call returned zero records, so no earlier study by this project on lineup role coverage is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether organizer, shaper, or terminal roles have been defined, validated, or tested before.
Whether role coverage is separable from talent or counts, or whether talent control works.
Any effect size, reliability estimate, or power figure for this question.
own_inferences: The question names three role categories but the task statement does not define them operationally. A definition based on play type, initiator, or points scored would be derived from the outcome being studied (OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL risk).

The stated 90 team-seasons matches three regular seasons times 30 teams (2022-23 to 2024-25). The 2025-26 data appear excluded from the count, and playoffs are not clearly represented, so the unit of analysis needs to be fixed before analysis.
Lineups are sparse within a team-season, so lineup-level role coverage estimates will be noisy and the within-team contrast may have few observations per lineup.

The data description lists no independent talent measure. Any talent proxy built from the same box score or play-by-play would be partly circular with role coverage, so talent control is not yet identifiable as described.
uncertainties: Operational definitions of organizer, shaper, and terminal are missing.
The derived play-type graph database is described but its schema and validation are not documented here.
Whether the 420,993 possessions cover regular season, playoffs, or both is unclear.
Reliability of role labels across seasons is unknown.
No historical record exists to calibrate expected effect sizes or the variance of role coverage within teams.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieval returned no records, so no historical finding, failed approach, or prior result altered the decision. The decision rests only on the task statement and the data description.

blocking_constraints.text: Organizer, shaper, and terminal are not operationally defined in the task; without validated definitions the role labels cannot be checked for accuracy.
Role labels built from play type, initiator, or points would partly encode the influence outcome they are meant to explain.
No independent talent measure is specified, so separating role coverage from talent and usage is not identifiable from the listed data.
Only about 90 team-seasons are available, which may give low power for within-team contrasts.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is unknown whether this question has been answered. No prior study is cited.

risks.text: Role definitions are not stated; misclassified players or lineups would bias every downstream coverage measure.
If roles use points or shot outcomes, coverage and influence are mechanically linked.
Talent, usage, and possession counts may drive both role coverage and lineup results; no clean talent control is specified.
Lineup-level role coverage may be unstable across games and seasons, so within-team variation may be measurement noise.
Many lineups have few possessions, and role combinations with all three roles may rarely occur.
Around 90 team-seasons limits power, especially once lineup and team fixed effects are included.
Three role types, several talent proxies, and several outcomes create many possible tests.
Roster and rule changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may shift role frequencies and talent relationships.
Using full-season role labels to explain in-season lineup outcomes would leak future information.

design.estimand: Within-team association between lineup role coverage (at least one organizer, shaper, or terminal on court) and lineup-level net rating per 100 possessions, adjusted for an independent talent measure. Not estimable until role definitions and the talent measure are fixed.
design.unit: Lineup-period (lineup within team-season, with possession counts), with team-season as the clustering unit.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 (90 team-seasons) as the primary sample. Playoffs and 2025-26 are held out for validation. Only lineups above a pre-registered possession threshold are included.
design.power: Compute a simulation-based power analysis before analysis, using the observed distribution of lineup possessions and an assumed within-team effect size. Report the minimum detectable effect; if it is implausibly large, stop.
design.controls: Independent talent proxy measured without the outcome (for example, prior-season or out-of-sample ratings), possession counts, minutes, lineup and team-season fixed effects, and role frequency per player. Roles must be defined before outcomes are viewed.
design.falsification: Role coverage should show no association with a placebo outcome (for example, free-throw rate or non-play-type events) and should not survive the talent control if it is only a proxy for talent. Test that the coverage measure is stable across split halves of each season.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary contrast. Apply Holm correction across any secondary role-type or outcome contrasts.
design.decision_rule: Proceed only if the pre-registered definitions are validated (split-half reliability and inter-rater agreement above a stated threshold), the simulated power for the primary effect is adequate, and the primary coefficient survives talent control and the placebo check. Otherwise report the question as untestable or uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons, with 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and playoffs as held-out validation. Fixed snapshot recorded at the time of analysis.
